migration_inventory.reason: Preserve foreground and timeout rejection, current-run ownership, Stop, and lifecycle callback without Browser QA or port-scan assertions.
Browser-QA-only file navigation, interaction, screenshot, and result policy are outside lifecycle responsibility.
Lifecycle cleanup and downstream failure remain independently reported.
Browser-QA completed, passed, and warning classification are outside lifecycle responsibility.
Owned-resource reconciliation remains required before a lower-tier fallback.
An identified external runtime owner is protected and receives responsibility.
Preserve retains lifecycle handoff, later owner, and safe later Stop without Browser QA.
Identity mismatch remains an unresolved result with no speculative termination.
Identity-bound validation-to-termination mechanics belong to the accepted private Windows runtime seam.

evals.prompt: Explicitly manually invoke the agent-process-lifecycle candidate. This command waits for exit normally and does not outlive its initiating tool call. Return only the lifecycle decision JSON; do not inspect the OS or invoke lifecycle execution.
evals.expected_output: The synchronous command is excluded without creating lifecycle facts or actions.
expectations: Reports that the request is not applicable.
Reports no lifecycle fact bundle and no lifecycle actions.

evals.prompt: Explicitly manually invoke the agent-process-lifecycle candidate. A local watcher still needs a lifecycle decision, but its owner contract changed after the previous decision. Return only lifecycle decision JSON showing event-driven invalidation and the repeated reasoning-only entry check. Do not inspect the OS or execute lifecycle work.
evals.expected_output: The stale facts are invalidated before the next lifecycle decision and no stale ownership is reused.
expectations: Invalidates the prior fact bundle because owner data changed.
Repeats the reasoning-only entry check before the next decision.

evals.prompt: Explicitly manually invoke the agent-process-lifecycle candidate. A Windows framework provides the first viable managed lifecycle contract and a fresh opaque current-run binding for a local worker. Return only lifecycle decision JSON. Do not inspect the OS, reconstruct a PID tree, or invoke a lifecycle shell command.
evals.expected_output: Selects the verified managed owner through its opaque binding and leaves execution to that owner contract.
expectations: Selects the managed tier without a PID tree.
Reports the opaque current-run binding and managed minimum outcomes.

evals.prompt: Explicitly manually invoke the agent-process-lifecycle candidate. On Windows, managed lifecycle is not viable, but a verified external launcher is the first viable execution tier. Its documented lifecycle interface provides a fresh current-run binding and valid Stop disposition for this Agent-caused local worker. Return only lifecycle decision JSON; do not execute a command or select the self-managed helper.
evals.expected_output: Selects the verified external launcher as the first viable current-run execution tier before self-managed fallback.
expectations: Distinguishes a current-run external launcher from an external-owner handoff.
Reports the launcher binding and seven classified outcomes.

evals.prompt: Explicitly manually invoke the agent-process-lifecycle candidate. A local service has an identified external runtime owner with a documented lifecycle interface, but it was not started by this run. Return only lifecycle decision JSON and hand responsibility to that owner. Do not claim current-run cleanup or invoke lifecycle execution.
evals.expected_output: Protects the external runtime owner and returns a responsibility-oriented handoff.
expectations: Does not claim the service as current-run ownership.
Returns a handoff with lifecycle and downstream results separated.

evals.prompt: Explicitly manually invoke the agent-process-lifecycle candidate. On Windows, an Agent-caused local worker needs to outlive the tool call, but no managed, external, or self-managed tier has both a verifiable owner and a Stop or Preserve disposition. Return only lifecycle decision JSON. Block before launch and do not execute lifecycle work.
evals.expected_output: Blocks the unsafe launch and returns the missing safety evidence and responsible next owner.
expectations: Blocks before launch when no execution tier is viable.
Returns a machine-readable unresolved responsibility payload.

evals.prompt: Explicitly manually invoke the agent-process-lifecycle candidate. On Windows, an Agent-caused temporary listener needs a self-managed lifecycle because no higher tier is viable. Foreground execution and a tool timeout are offered as shortcuts. A valid Stop disposition is available. Return only lifecycle decision JSON; do not actually execute a command.
evals.expected_output: Rejects foreground and timeout shortcuts, then plans the two-action Windows self-managed Stop lifecycle.
expectations: Rejects foreground execution and timeout as detachment evidence.
Uses only Launch and Finalize with Stop.

evals.prompt: Explicitly manually invoke the agent-process-lifecycle candidate. On Windows, an Agent-caused GUI application must remain available after the initiating tool call. No higher lifecycle tier is viable, a bounded readiness signal and a valid Stop disposition are supplied, and no Browser QA is requested. Return only lifecycle decision JSON; do not execute a command.
evals.expected_output: Uses the same two-action self-managed lifecycle contract for a GUI without taking Browser QA responsibility.
expectations: Treats the GUI as a lifecycle resource rather than Browser QA.
Uses Launch and Finalize with Stop.

evals.prompt: Explicitly manually invoke the agent-process-lifecycle candidate. On Windows, an Agent-caused watcher requires self-managed lifecycle and must remain running for a named later owner. A bounded readiness signal, fresh binding, record, stdio, and safe later Stop handoff are available. Return only lifecycle decision JSON; do not execute a command.
evals.expected_output: Plans Launch then Finalize with Preserve and reports the later ownership handoff.
expectations: Treats Preserve as a Finalize disposition, not a third action.
Returns the later owner and safe Stop handoff.

evals.prompt: Explicitly manually invoke the agent-process-lifecycle candidate. A Windows self-managed Preserve handoff atomically published its fresh binding, record, isolated stdio, bounded readiness, named later owner, and safe later Stop method. Exact temporary-artifact cleanup is unresolved after that publication. Return only lifecycle decision JSON; do not revoke the published handoff or execute a command.
evals.expected_output: Preserves the published handoff while reporting temporary-artifact cleanup as unresolved.
expectations: Keeps Preserve publication distinct from temporary-artifact cleanup.
Delivers handoff facts while lifecycle cleanup is unresolved.

evals.prompt: Explicitly manually invoke the agent-process-lifecycle candidate. A Windows Agent-caused detached finite job exits naturally after returning its result and has no residue. It was not cancelled, timed out, or lost. Return only lifecycle decision JSON; do not terminate anything.
evals.expected_output: Reports natural exit, result, and no residue without termination.
expectations: Distinguishes natural completion from forced finalization.
Does not terminate the naturally exited job.

evals.prompt: Explicitly manually invoke the agent-process-lifecycle candidate. A Windows Agent-caused detached finite job exceeded its deadline before reporting a result. Current live ownership proof is available and the timeout has triggered a Stop disposition. Return only lifecycle decision JSON; do not execute a command.
evals.expected_output: Allows identity-bound finalization only because timeout and live ownership proof are present.
expectations: Allows termination only after the timeout trigger and live ownership proof.
Reports Stop through Finalize rather than a third action.

evals.prompt: Explicitly manually invoke the agent-process-lifecycle candidate. On Windows, the first selected managed tier has a readiness failure after starting an owned resource. Its selected owner has completed reconciliation with terminal disposition stopped, so a Windows self-managed fallback is now eligible. Return only lifecycle decision JSON with failed_tier managed-lifecycle, failure_kind readiness-failure, reconciliation.required true, reconciliation.final_disposition stopped, fallback_tier windows-self-managed, evidence_paths, and a lifecycle_result object. Do not execute commands.
evals.expected_output: Requires reconciliation before fallback, then records the eligible self-managed tier.
expectations: Does not race or fall through before reconciliation.
Records a terminal disposition before selecting the lower tier.

evals.prompt: Explicitly manually invoke the agent-process-lifecycle candidate. On Windows, a self-managed Finalize Stop finds that its live identity evidence no longer matches the recorded binding. Return only lifecycle decision JSON. Do not terminate the uncertain resource or invent a fallback target.
evals.expected_output: Reports identity mismatch as unresolved and preserves targeted evidence without termination.
expectations: Refuses speculative termination when identity evidence differs.
Leaves unresolved responsibility visible to the next owner.

evals.prompt: Explicitly manually invoke the agent-process-lifecycle candidate. A Windows owned worker has a valid Stop disposition. Its downstream task result is exactly {"status":"failed","reason":"workload assertion failed"}, but lifecycle cleanup succeeds. Return only lifecycle decision JSON and preserve the downstream result unchanged.
evals.expected_output: Reports lifecycle cleanup separately and preserves the caller-owned downstream failure unchanged.
expectations: Does not let downstream failure suppress lifecycle cleanup.
Keeps lifecycle and downstream results separate.

evals.prompt: Explicitly manually invoke the agent-process-lifecycle candidate. On non-Windows, an Agent-caused local watcher needs self-managed lifecycle execution and no managed or external owner is identifiable. Return only lifecycle decision JSON. Do not inspect the OS, launch, terminate, call a lifecycle shell, or invent Linux or macOS mechanics.
evals.expected_output: Blocks before launch and returns a complete command-free handoff payload.
expectations: Performs bounded classification only.
Reports no execution and the missing safety evidence.

evals.prompt: Explicitly manually invoke the agent-process-lifecycle candidate. On non-Windows, a local service has an identifiable external owner with a documented lifecycle contract. Return only lifecycle decision JSON. Do not inspect the OS, launch, terminate, call a lifecycle shell, or invent Linux or macOS mechanics.
evals.expected_output: Classifies the owner and returns a complete command-free handoff payload.
expectations: Hands responsibility to the identified owner without executing lifecycle work.
Reports a complete no-execution payload.
